To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) acute alcohol impairs macrophages in their capacity to clear apoptotic cells by suppressing the expression of the protein MFG-E8; 2) chronic alcohol enhances the expression of the pro-inflammatory protein HMGB1 in serum and attenuates efferocytotic activity by macrophages.

acute alcohol exposure inhibits efferocytotic capacity of macrophages via suppression of MFG-E 8 gene expression through reactive oxygen species dependent mechanisms, and this effect can be blocked by the antioxidant NAC.

acute alcohol exposure attenuates macrophage eferrocytosis via inhibition on MFG-E8 through ROS dependent mechanism, while chronic alcohol exposure promotes macrophage eefrocytosis by enhancing MFG-E8 but attenuated by HMGB1 in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying alcohol-induced impairment of macrophage eferocytosis.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the effects of alcohol on efferocytotic activity of macrophages.
the molecular mechanism underlying alcohol-induced impairment of macrophage effector function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

acute alcohol exposure inhibits macrophage eferocytosis via a reactive oxygen species-dependent mechanism that involves inhibition of MFG8 gene expression, and that chronic alcohol exposure enhances macrophage effocytosis by upregulation of MFG-E gene expression, but the effect is attenuated by HMGB1.
alcohol exposure impairs efferocytotic function of macrophages through MFG-E8/HMGB1 pathway.
alcohol-induced efferocytotic dysfunction is a consequence of a balance between MFG8 and HMGB-1 levels.

acute alcohol exposure inhibits macrophage eferrocytosis through suppression of MFG-E 8 gene expression and chronic alcohol exposure enhances efferocytotic activity of macrophages through up-regulation of MFG-E-8 gene expression, which might be counteracted by HMGB1.

The main takeaway from our work is that
alcohol affects macrophage eferocytosis through a complex mechanism.
the balance between HMGB1 and MFG-E8 levels is critical to the outcome of alcohol-induced alteration of macrophage effector functions in vivo.
alcohol exposure alters macrophage eferrocytosis by modulating the levels of two key molecules, MFG-E8, and HMGB1, which have opposite effects on efferocytotic process.
